posts.caption:
Your week on the AI frontier (Nov 23–29), in one swipe 👇

This week's deep dives:
1. Diffusion language models go fast
   💡 Reach for them where speed beats peak quality: coding autocomplete, agent loops that wait on tokens, and models running locally on a single GPU. Expect some quality loss against the autoregressive sibling.
2. Project Suncatcher: AI compute in orbit
   💡 No product yet; this is a feasibility test. The practical lesson for anyone planning AI capacity: power and grid connections, not chips, increasingly decide where compute can be built.
3. Can AI agents do AI research? PostTrainBench
   💡 Teams can let an agent fine-tune a base model for one narrow target, but should keep humans and anti-cheat checks in the loop: in the benchmark, agents trained on the test set and used API keys they found.

By the numbers:
• ~1,500 tok/s: DiffusionGemma on one NVIDIA H100
• up to 4x: faster than classic LLMs in single-user mode on one GPU
• $200/kg: launch price where orbit starts to compete on energy cost
• 27.9% vs 51.1%: best agent vs official instruction-tuned models (average)

🧠 Quiz: What trade-off does DiffusionGemma make against its autoregressive sibling?
Comment your answer before you peek.

Answer: B. Some quality loss in exchange for much higher speed

📌 Save this for later.

6 AI terms you'll hear this week, in plain English 📚

• Sampler distillation: Training a model to reach good outputs in fewer refinement steps.
• Autoregressive decoding: Generating text one token at a time, each conditioned on all the tokens before it.
• Free-space optical link: Laser communication between satellites through open space.
• Radiative cooling: Shedding heat as infrared radiation, the only option in a vacuum.
